header.title: How to Remove Corrosion from Copper Wiring
header.description: This guide provides a step-by-step process for removing corrosion (copper oxide) from copper wiring using a homemade cleaning solution and neutralization process. It details how to prepare cleaning and neutralizing agents and safely apply them to restore the wire's conductivity.

steps.description: Before cleaning copper wire, strip the insulation back far enough to ensure all corrosion is removed and identify tinned wires.
actions: Understand the problem of oxidation and its effect on copper wire.
Strip the insulation far enough back.
Inspect the wire for corrosion.
Identify tinned (silvery) copper wires.

steps.description: This step involves creating a cleaning solution of vinegar and salt to remove patina from copper wiring.
actions: Put one tablespoon of salt in the first container.
Fill the rest of the container with vinegar.
Stir the solution together.
Add salt to the container until the solution no longer dissolves it.

steps.description: Create a neutralizing solution by mixing sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and water in a container.
actions: Put one tablespoon of Sodium Bicarbonate in the second container
Finish filling the container with water
Stir together
Add more baking soda as needed
Stir the mixture

steps.description: Clean the exposed copper of the wire by submerging it in a vinegar solution and stirring.
actions: Dip the end of the wire or wires in the vinegar solution
Ensure the stripped exposed copper is completely submerged
Stir the solution with the wire
Keep stirring the wire in the solution until it becomes uniformly shiny

steps.description: Submerge the cleaned wire in a neutralizing solution and stir to remove any remaining acid.
actions: Pull the wire out of the container
Submerge the copper completely inside the neutralizing solution
Stir the solution for 10 or 15 seconds
